evals.name: full-pipeline-bun-tdd
evals.prompt: I want a reusable workflow for building features in this repo, run by an agent orchestrator (a workflow lead) step by step. My flow: work in a git worktree cut from the current branch; bun install to bootstrap; first a user-story interview with me, then a spec with gherkin acceptance criteria, an automated spec review with fixes, and I sign off on the spec exactly once; implementation in vertical slices, strict TDD, with a quick review of every slice; after all slices, one exhaustive engineering review; then a final definition-of-done validation; finish with the branch left ready for me to open the PR myself. The quality gates I want are exactly the ones listed — the per-slice reviews, the one exhaustive review, and the DoD validation. Create the whole thing: the workflow file, the agents it needs, any scripts, and a way to launch it. I'm away from the keyboard after sending this — where I haven't specified something, go with your recommended default and complete the package in this session.
evals.expected_output: A workflow package: workflows/<name>/<name>.yaml with tiny nodes (install as its own node, story loop, spec loop with Format: gherkin, spec review + fixes, single approval loop, TDD slice loop with quick per-slice review, exhaustive review round, DoD settle, PR-ready finish — worktree created by the launch script, not a YAML node), agents/ with workflow_lead + the referenced agents, running.md execution contract, README, launchers for Claude Code, Codex and opencode, and an executable ./<name>.sh — all written in positive terms.
expectations: package-structure: a workflow package directory exists containing a YAML workflow file, an agents/ folder with a workflow-lead agent file, and launcher files for all three hosts — .claude/commands/<name>.md, .codex/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and .opencode/command/<name>.md — each pointing at the same workflow with the same input mapping
yaml-valid-simple-nodes: the workflow YAML parses, and every node has an id and exactly one behavior (a command, an agent invocation with a prompt, a loop, or a human gate)
no-multiline-inline-shell: no command in any node or loop step contains a newline or chained multi-step shell logic — anything bigger is a script file

worktree-via-launch-script: an executable repo-root .sh named after the workflow plus a sibling agents-cli.conf create or reuse a git worktree and start claude, codex, or opencode inside it; bun install is its own YAML node; the workflow YAML contains no git worktree command and no workdir key
loops-bounded-and-exitable: every loop declares max_iterations and exactly one explicit exit condition (a completion signal or a command-based check)

agent-steps-carry-required-args: every agent invocation passes the arguments its agent definition requires (e.g. verification commands for implementer/reviewer steps, a base ref for the engineering review, a format for the spec step)
gherkin-format-requested: the spec-writing step explicitly requests Gherkin acceptance criteria
tdd-not-split-pairing: the slice build loop uses a strict-TDD implementer that owns both tests and code, and does NOT also include a separate unit-test-writer agent in that loop

phases-match-request: the node sequence includes a user-story interview loop, a spec + automated spec review + fix step, exactly one human spec sign-off, a slice loop with a quick per-slice review, exactly one exhaustive engineering review after all slices, and a DoD validation — and contains NO mutation-testing and NO push/PR-opening node
execution-contract-shipped: the package includes a running/execution-contract document that defines the node semantics for the lead (with the skill: a verbatim copy of the skill's assets/running.md)
quiet-commands: test/check commands in the YAML prefer failure-only or quiet output variants (e.g. bun test --only-failures, install --silent)
referenced-files-exist: every agent path and script path referenced by the YAML exists in the package, and scripts are executable

positive-phrasing: the generated artifacts (README, YAML comments, agent prompts) describe every decision in positive terms — what the workflow does — with no negation echoes such as 'no worktree', 'non-gherkin', 'NOT TDD', 'no mutation testing', or 'ruled out'

agents-scoped-to-workflow: every packaged agent copy is tailored to this workflow — no agent carries a mode no node invokes, and none checks an artifact no node produces (in particular, the DoD/validation agent makes no reference to mutation artifacts, since this workflow has no mutation step)

evals.name: docs-workflow-agnostic
evals.prompt: This repo is our markdown docs site. I want a workflow an agent lead can run step by step: given a page id and a rough ask, an outline interview with me (one question at a time) to settle the outline; then a writer agent drafts the page under docs/; then an edit loop — an editor agent reviews the draft and the writer fixes findings — capped at 3 rounds; then a link-check script I want written (checks that relative markdown links in docs/ resolve); and finally I approve the page before the run ends. Work on the current branch. The only automated check in this repo is the link-check script you'll write. Please create the workflow file, the agents, the script, and a launcher. I'm away while you build this — use your best recommendations for anything unspecified and complete the package in this session.
evals.expected_output: A non-code workflow package proving the creator is domain-agnostic: runs in place on the current branch, an interview loop, newly authored writer + editor agents following the design rules (agnostic, isolated, one return line), an edit loop capped at 3, a single-purpose executable link-check script as its own node, a final gate, and the standard package skeleton (yaml, running.md, workflow_lead, README, launcher) — all written in positive terms.
expectations: package-structure: a workflow package directory exists containing a YAML workflow file, an agents/ folder with a workflow-lead agent file, and launcher files for all three hosts — .claude/commands/<name>.md, .codex/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and .opencode/command/<name>.md — each pointing at the same workflow with the same input mapping
yaml-valid-simple-nodes: the workflow YAML parses, and every node has an id and exactly one behavior (a command, an agent invocation with a prompt, a loop, or a human gate)
current-branch-no-worktree: the workflow runs in place — no worktree/workdir setup, no git worktree command anywhere, and no repo-root launch script
no-code-pipeline-baggage: the workflow contains no test, typecheck, build, CI, or mutation nodes — the repo has none of those
outline-interview-loop: the outline interview is a bounded loop designed for one-question-per-turn relay to the human, with a completion signal

new-agents-follow-design-rules: writer and editor are two separate newly authored agent files, each with name+description frontmatter, a single-line return convention with an explicit signal, arguments passed via invocation (not baked-in repo facts), and neither referencing the other agent by name
edit-loop-capped-at-3: the editor-reviews/writer-fixes loop has max_iterations 3 and an explicit exit condition

linkcheck-script-single-purpose: the link-check script exists in the package, is executable, does exactly one thing (verify relative markdown links in docs/ resolve), is invoked by its own dedicated node, and works when actually executed — a clean pass on the repo's docs and a reported failure on an injected broken link
final-human-approval: a human approval gate (or interactive approval loop) is the last meaningful step before the run ends
no-multiline-inline-shell: no command in any node or loop step contains a newline or chained multi-step shell logic
execution-contract-shipped: the package includes a running/execution-contract document that defines the node semantics for the lead (with the skill: a verbatim copy of the skill's assets/running.md)

positive-phrasing: the generated artifacts (README, YAML comments, agent prompts) describe every decision in positive terms — what the workflow does — with no negation echoes such as 'no worktree', 'no build', or 'ruled out'

evals.name: mutation-split-pairing
evals.prompt: Set up a feature workflow for this Bun/TypeScript repo that a workflow-lead agent executes node by node. Requirements: run on the current branch. Spec phase: plain acceptance criteria, an automated spec review, and a single human approval of the spec. Build in vertical slices, with production code and unit tests owned by two independent agents — an implementer that owns only the production code, and a unit-test writer that owns only the tests — plus a quick review each slice. After the build: a full engineering review capped at 2 rounds, then mutation testing with StrykerJS scoped to the changed files, capped at 3 rounds — the mutation loop's exit must be decided solely by a script reading Stryker's own log. Then a definition-of-done validation. The .awc task trail should be committed with the work. Create everything: workflow file, agents, scripts, launcher. Use recommended defaults for the rest; I'm offline until tomorrow, so make your recommended calls and complete the package in this session.
evals.expected_output: A package using the split pairing (implementer + unit_test_writer), quick slice reviews, an engineering review round capped at 2 with CI steps around it, a mutation round capped at 3 ending on until_run with a strict gate script that reads Stryker's log, mutation_tester invoked with the log path, dod settle loop, running in place on the current branch, and the standard package skeleton — all written in positive terms.
expectations: package-structure: a workflow package directory exists containing a YAML workflow file, an agents/ folder with a workflow-lead agent file, and launcher files for all three hosts — .claude/commands/<name>.md, .codex/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and .opencode/command/<name>.md — each pointing at the same workflow with the same input mapping
yaml-valid-simple-nodes: the workflow YAML parses, and every node has an id and exactly one behavior (a command, an agent invocation with a prompt, a loop, or a human gate)
current-branch-no-worktree: the workflow runs in place — no worktree/workdir setup, no git worktree command anywhere, and no repo-root launch script
split-pairing-not-tdd: the slice loop uses an implementer (production code only) AND a separate unit-test writer (tests only) as independent steps — no strict-TDD self-contained implementer
plain-format-and-single-approval: the spec step requests plain acceptance criteria, an automated spec review runs before the human, and there is exactly one human spec sign-off

review-round-verified-tree: the engineering review loop is capped at 2, the reviewer receives a base ref, never runs CI itself, and the round has a CI/check command step before the reviewer and again after the fix step

mutation-exit-is-a-script: the mutation loop is capped at 3 and exits via a command/script check (until_run or equivalent) whose script reads the mutation tool's own log or report output — never an agent-emitted completion signal — and the gate is strict: any surviving or uncovered mutant fails it (a lenient default threshold such as 80% must not pass it)

mutation-reporter-gets-log: the mutation-report agent step receives the path to the captured mutation log in its invocation, and a preceding node runs Stryker scoped to changed files capturing that log

mutation-fixes-routed: the mutation loop routes fixes to the right owners — production-defect kills to the implementer, test-side kills to the unit-test writer — and re-runs checks before the next mutation round
dod-settle-loop: a DoD validation step receives the check commands and a base ref, in a bounded loop with fix step(s) after it
scripts-single-purpose: every generated script does exactly one thing, is executable, and no node hides multi-step shell logic inline
execution-contract-shipped: the package includes a running/execution-contract document that defines the node semantics for the lead (with the skill: a verbatim copy of the skill's assets/running.md)
quiet-commands: test/check commands prefer failure-only or quiet output variants (e.g. bun test --only-failures)

positive-phrasing: the generated artifacts (README, YAML comments, agent prompts) describe every decision in positive terms — what the workflow does — with no negation echoes such as 'no worktree', 'non-gherkin', 'NOT TDD', or 'ruled out'

agents-scoped-to-workflow: every packaged agent copy is tailored to this workflow — no agent carries a mode no node invokes and none checks an artifact no node produces (e.g. if there is no post-mutation delta-review node, the engineering reviewer ships without a delta-review mode)
